findings.title: Workflow level directly instantiates Agent
findings.description: Level1Rapid imports and directly instantiates WriterAgent inside execute(), creating tight coupling between workflow and agent layers. This violates the Dependency Inversion Principle.
findings.recommendation: Inject agents via constructor or use ServiceContainer to resolve agent dependencies. Workflow levels should depend on agent abstractions, not concrete implementations.

findings.title: Multiple agent instantiations in workflow level
findings.description: Level3Standard directly instantiates ArchitectAgent, WriterAgent, and CriticAgent in _plan_phase, _execute_phase, and _critic_phase methods. Each invocation creates new instances without lifecycle management.
findings.recommendation: Use dependency injection via ServiceContainer. Pass pre-configured agent instances or use factory pattern to centralize agent creation.

findings.title: Memory layer depends on Search layer
findings.description: CoreMemoryStore imports VectorSearch from search module using relative import `from ..search.vector_search`. This creates a horizontal dependency between peer modules.
findings.recommendation: Consider extracting VectorSearch interface to a shared protocols module, or inject VectorSearch as a dependency rather than importing directly.

findings.title: Service layer imports from Agent layer
findings.description: DistillService imports BaseAgent from agents layer. Services should not depend on agent implementations.
findings.recommendation: If only using BaseAgent for Prompt Protocol, extract the protocol to a shared module. Services should remain independent of agent layer.

findings.title: Container properties return Any type
findings.description: All engine properties (memory, graph, search, workflow, critic, commander, writer) return `Any` type. This eliminates type safety benefits and IDE autocompletion.
findings.recommendation: Define Protocol/Interface types for each engine and use proper return type annotations. Example: `def memory(self) -> IMemoryEngine:`

findings.title: Configuration loading mixed with DI container
findings.description: _load_gateway_engine_config defines inline dataclasses and loads configuration. This mixes configuration concerns with dependency injection responsibilities.
findings.recommendation: Extract EnginePluginConfig and GatewayEngineConfig to a dedicated config module. Container should only handle dependency resolution.

findings.title: BaseAgent handles too many responsibilities
findings.description: BaseAgent combines prompt construction (CCW 6-Field Protocol), token counting, cost estimation, budget control, and usage tracking. This violates Single Responsibility Principle.
findings.recommendation: Extract TokenCostEstimator and BudgetController to separate utility classes. BaseAgent should focus on agent abstraction and prompt building.

findings.title: Inconsistent config type annotation
findings.description: get_default_config returns BaseWorkflowConfig but returns a dict literal. BaseWorkflowConfig is likely a TypeAlias for Dict, creating confusion.
findings.recommendation: Use explicit TypedDict or dataclass for configuration. Ensure type annotations match actual return types.

findings.title: MCP Gateway imports from multiple layers
findings.description: Gateway imports from container, workflow.base_state, workflow.levels, knowledge.services, and config. While expected for an entry point, the import list is extensive.
findings.recommendation: Consider a facade pattern to reduce direct dependencies. Gateway should orchestrate through a smaller set of high-level interfaces.

findings.title: Duplicate CriticEngine implementations
findings.description: CriticEngine exists in both src/narrative/critic_engine.py and src/narrative/evaluators/critic_engine.py. The agents/critic.py imports from evaluators version.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate to single CriticEngine implementation. Remove duplicate or clearly differentiate responsibilities if both are needed.

layers.name: agents
layers.role: Agent abstraction, prompt building, LLM interaction

layers.name: workflow
layers.role: L1-L5 workflow levels, adapters, session management

strengths: Clear layer separation with distinct responsibilities
Lazy loading and plugin system in ServiceContainer
Consistent use of dataclasses for DTOs
weaknesses: Workflow levels tightly coupled to agent implementations
Lack of type safety in container (Any return types)
